content:
Based on last sentence in https://www.openstreetmap.org/note/5617596 and recent track at https://www.mapillary.com/app/?pKey=1625166192349556 (and forward), I think that R1 veloroute is wrong.
I think it should go something like in this picture:

Reasoning:
I think that those 857. signs seen in mapillary track and later 417. sign at pedestrian part of Torņa iela, imply that R1 should go there, in direction of mapillary track.
In reverse, I believe route should go right after pedestrian bridge , along the cycleway to theatre and to Vanšu tilts.

And outside Vecrīga there is a cycle infrastructure running to same Gaisma tilt outside of Brīvības. So it would make sense for route to run along that infra.

If you have any information I'm missing or a different opinion - please share.

857. Velomaršruts
417. Kopīgs gājēju un velosipēdu ceļš

So those 857. signs are not part of the actual Euroroute stuff. So they don't really mean anything as far as the official route layout goes. So the route we choose should be official unless we know it's outdated, in which case we can probably route it along the proper infrastructure. And that's where the 857. signs can sway our decision. I just don't know what the Euro routes are intending to include. Like do they actually want you to go past the Freedom Monument? Like is this part of the route? Because if you just move it to some side street, you basically skip all of the Old Riga. I really haven't done the research. It's the similar question around https://www.openstreetmap.org/note/5622066 - Is the route supposed to go to Mežgarciems for its historical stuff? Or is this just the way that was available before the cycleway?

857. Velomaršruts
Note: 5622066
OpenStreetMap is a map of the world, created by people like you and free to use under an open license.

I don't really have the time to do this research. But I imagine I would look at the official routes and actually see what their history is and what they intended to show you. Because if they have like "Freedom Monument - waypoint #84" then we cannot reroute it like this. But if it's just a general passthrough route and you're responsible for making your own exploration...

But there are no separate Euroroute signs, right?
Like 858. are EuroVelo, not euroroute.

858. "EuroVelo" maršruts

HellMap said:

I don't really have the time to do this research. But I imagine I would look at the official routes and actually see what their history is and what they intended to show you. Because if they have like "Freedom Monument - waypoint #84" then we cannot reroute it like this. But if it's just a general passthrough route and you're responsible for making your own exploration...

That's also a problem, because I really can't find anything good about R1. It's mostly only german part.

I don't think there are separate signs. So these may have been intended for this. But there is no official guidance, so who knows what they mean? I have seen them placed in completely random locations where there are no routes. And I have to see them placed along rounds. So it feels very random. And I think it's a judgment call. Like the Mapillary example you gave is probably where the route should go? But then it should go there both ways, not just one way, right?

Like I'm pretty sure these routes existed before half the cycleways and signage existed in Riga. Like half the sidewalks and footways here were never intended to be cycleways. They didn't actually rebuild anything, they just added a couple new sections and then just plopped a bunch of signs. I don't know if anyone actually considered any of the big routes for this.
I think in the opposite direction route goes in a different way: along Zigfrida Anna Mierovica to theatre, and then to bridge.
Does the actual official route does this? Well, I don't know. This is all very complicated, so good luck.

One hour later I'm not one hour wiser.
As far as I can tell - there is no real "official" route for Latvia. Which probably shouldn't be surprising, since it can't even decide itself where it ends: in Moscow, St.Petersburg or Helsinki =)

I'll update route to make it as reasonable as possible.
Wiki is probably old though, don't they have a website?
That site only has german map/tracks/pois and a couple of articles about western other countries, but nothing about Baltics three at all.

Yeah, this route seems completely vague. I'm honestly not ever sure anymore why OSM is even mapping it. It cannot even agree on the cities it goes through. I bet the only reason it exists is because in Germany it's better defined.

I update route.
But I will be completely fine if it were to be deleted later, if nobody cares for its existence.
Has anybody contacted the maintainers? We discussed it years ago, don't recall the outcome.
Sorry, maintainers of what?
I don't remember this being discussed, so this must have been somewhere else. There were no updates to wiki guidelines or anything as far as I know.

markalex said:

Sorry, maintainers of what?

Pieņemu, ka https://www.europaradweg-r1.de/ - lai gan tur Baltijas valstis tikai pieminētas pie joprojām eksistējošas sadaļas "finale in St. Petersburg" (pat tad, ja kāds būtu pilnīgi negudrs, pēc trim dienām par to posmu varēs pilnībā aizmirst).
Varbūt mēs varam izlemt, kur to prātīgāk aizmaršrutēt, sazīmēt, un aizsūtīt viņiem. Lai tiek galā :)

Tas man liekas ir pa traku. Mēs viņu maršrutu zīmējam, jo viņi paši to nekur nav ievadījuši. Un vēl mēs labosim viņiem, jo viņi pat nevar salikt aptuveni? Es uzskatu, ka tādi maršrutu veidotāji iztiks. Mums ir pietiekami ar 100iem vietējo maršrutu, kuri jālabo.

Viņiem bija GPX lapā laikam.
Bet nebiju domājis tur super analizēt - ja kaut kur mums šķiet tizli vai mainījušas velojoslas ielās (un maršruts sanāk vai nu nelegāls, vai ļoti neērts), to posmiņu tikai pabīdām vai nu uz blakus ielu, uz parku vai ko taml. Piekrītu, ka citādi šim jau ļoti daudz laika veltīts.
Te jau tā lieta, ka nekāds GPX nebija. Tur biju burtiksi tikai pilsēta ierakstīta un viss. https://www.europaradweg-r1.de/service-informationen/gpx-track-downloads tikai Vācijā
